ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Bilateral (predominantly right) knee pain with clicking during and after running/work-outs.
• Symptom details: Began ~2 weeks ago after increasing run distance for marathon training; pain starts ≈20 min / ~3 mi into run, sometimes forces her to stop; occasional clicking during leg-extension/ab work; once noticed mild swelling that resolved with ice; single episode of right-toe tingling post-run; no locking, giving-way, or constant pain; full range of motion; no baseline swelling, redness, fever.
• Past medical history: Hyperopia (LASIK), prior significant UTI/possible renal colic; remote right knee contusion from ice-hockey fall months ago; otherwise healthy.
• Medications/allergies: Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, Aleve (naproxen) PRN, vitamin D, melatonin, occasional Xanax; smokes marijuana joints; no allergies reported.
• Family/social history: Active—ice hockey, regular gym, currently marathon training; lives in London; no smoking/tobacco or alcohol history stated; occasional marijuana use.
• Vital signs/exam findings (video only): No current swelling, erythema, or warmth; right knee pain localized “middle then slightly to the right”; full flexion/extension; clicking with gym leg movements; able to walk, climb stairs without pain; no calf tenderness, colour change, or temperature change in legs; mild sock indentation oedema after prolonged standing.
• Labs/imaging: None performed yet.

V: Deep venous thrombosis: Could give unilateral calf/knee discomfort and toe tingling, but absence of persistent swelling, calf pain, or risk factors makes it unlikely.
I: Septic arthritis / acute inflammatory arthritis: Would present with swollen, hot, painful joint and systemic features—currently not present but kept in mind if swelling/fever develop.
Prepatellar bursitis: Overuse or kneeling can inflame bursa and cause anterior knee pain/swelling; transient swelling described.
N: Bone/soft-tissue neoplasm (e.g., osteoid osteoma, synovial sarcoma): Chronic, progressive pain usually unrelated to activity; no red-flag features but theoretically possible.
D: Patellofemoral pain syndrome (chondromalacia patella): Classic overuse injury in runners causing anterior knee pain, clicking, aggravated by running, squatting, stairs.
Early degenerative meniscal tear: Can cause pain and clicking; prior hockey fall could be inciting trauma.
Patellar tendinopathy (jumper’s knee): Overuse of extensor mechanism with pain worsened by running and leg extension.
I2: NSAID-induced gastritis/ulcer (iatrogenic) – relevant to treatment plan but not cause of knee pain.
C: Congenital patellar maltracking/ hypermobility: Could predispose to patellofemoral pain in active patient.
A: Early rheumatoid arthritis or other autoimmune arthropathy: Less likely given mono-articular, activity-related pain and lack of stiffness, swelling.
T: Anterior cruciate ligament or medial collateral ligament sprain/tear: Patient worried about ACL; remote fall and current running could strain ligaments, but no instability or giving-way reported.
Iliotibial band syndrome: Overuse friction causing lateral knee pain after running.
E: Vitamin D deficiency–related bone/joint pain: She supplements vitamin D; presentation activity-linked.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Patellofemoral pain syndrome (runner’s knee / chondromalacia patella)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Most common cause of anterior knee pain in young runners; provoked by increased mileage, characterized by pain after prolonged running, clicking with flexion/extension, and usually normal exam aside from retropatellar tenderness (not tested here).
supporting_evidence: Onset after increasing run distance for marathon training
Pain starts ~20 min into run and with leg-extension exercises
No locking, instability, or consistent swelling
opposing_evidence: Pain described as ‘middle then right side’ rather than classic anterior location
Single prior swelling episode (PFPS usually non-swollen)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Overuse of the extensor mechanism from running and gym work can inflame patellar tendon causing pain with activity and clicking sensations.
supporting_evidence: Activity-related pain, worse with running and leg extension exercises
opposing_evidence: Pain location not clearly inferior to patella/tendon described

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Prior knee trauma (hockey fall) plus new repetitive running could aggravate a meniscal tear, producing pain and mechanical symptoms like clicking.
supporting_evidence: History of knee trauma months ago
Pain that worsens during longer runs
opposing_evidence: No locking, giving-way, or inability to fully extend/flex
Currently no effusion; meniscal tears often present with persistent swelling

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Common runner overuse injury causing lateral knee pain after certain mileage.
supporting_evidence: Pain may ‘move to the right side of knee’
opposing_evidence: No tenderness over lateral femoral epicondyle reported

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Could stem from prior hockey fall but typically causes instability or acute swelling, which she denies.
supporting_evidence: Patient concern due to reading about ACL; history of fall
opposing_evidence: No giving-way, instability, or acute swelling
Able to run and perform activities until pain starts
